chunks: Al-Qāsim ibn Burayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who set up a net in the water, then returned to his house and left it set up. Then he came back to it after that, and fish had fallen into it and died. So he said: “What his hand has done, then there is no harm in eating what fell into it.”

key_terms.شَبَكَةً: a fishing net set to catch fish
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.فَمُوِّتْنَ: they died after being caught in it
key_terms.مَا عَمِلَتْ يَدُهُ: what was brought about by his own direct action
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءِ: the water in which the net was placed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish that died in a net after being caught and left unattended?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about fish caught in a net that was set by a person and later found with dead fish in it. The Imam عليه السلام states that since the catching occurred through the person’s own act, there is no harm in eating the fish caught in that manner.
